ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in rectangle $ABCD$, we have $AD=1$, $AB>1$, and $AG$ bisects $\angle BAD$. Perpendiculars are drawn from points B and C to $AG$ at points E and F, respectively. What is the value of $\left(AE-GF\right)$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Let AE = x,

since quadrilateral ABCD is a rectangle,

therefore, $\angle BAD = \angle D = 90^\circ$, CD = AB,

since AG bisects $\angle BAD$,

therefore, $\angle DAG = 45^\circ$,

therefore, $\triangle ADG$ is an isosceles right triangle,

therefore, DG = AD = 1,

therefore, AG = $\sqrt{2}$AD = $\sqrt{2}$,

Similarly: BE = AE = x, CD = AB = $\sqrt{2}x$,

therefore, CG = CD - DG = $\sqrt{2}x - 1$,

Similarly: CG = $\sqrt{2}$FG,

therefore, FG = $\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}$CG = x - $\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}$,

therefore, AE - GF = x - (x - $\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}$) = $\boxed{\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}}$.

Because in the rectangle ∠BAD=90°, and AG bisects this angle, AG makes 45° with both AB and AD, and its equation is y=x. AG intersects the line y=1 on which the upper side CD lies at G=(1,1). The foot of the perpendicular from point B=(b,0) to the line y=x is E. Projecting onto y=x gives E=(b/2,b/2), so the length of AE is sqrt((b/2)^2+(b/2)^2)=b/sqrt(2). The foot of the perpendicular from point C=(b,1) to the line y=x is F. Projecting onto y=x gives F=((b+1)/2,(b+1)/2). G=(1,1), so GF is the distance on the line y=x from (1,1) to ((b+1)/2,(b+1)/2), namely sqrt(2)*((b+1)/2-1)=(b-1)/sqrt(2). Therefore AE-GF=b/sqrt(2)-(b-1)/sqrt(2)=1/sqrt(2)=sqrt(2)/2.
